title: All-continuous Omega comparison for uniform supported-image upper bounds
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites in the small indexing universe [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. A support chain over $X$ means a finite chain $S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0=X$, where each arrow is a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a condensed coefficient ring $R$, put $R_T=p_T^*R$ and $\mathcal A_{R,T}=\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}$. Write $J_R=J_{R,1}\circ\cdots\circ J_{R,r}$, where $J_{R,t}=(a_t)_!$ in the open case and $J_{R,t}=(a_t)_*$ in the closed case [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. For an affine pro-étale object $v:U\to X$, set $F_{R,v}=v^*J_R$. The empty chain has $J_R=\mathrm{id}$. All derived categories and $R\Gamma$ are the ordinary uncompleted module-derived ones, with section complexes valued in abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Put $R_\Omega(P)=\{c\in C(P,\Omega):c(P)\subseteq E\text{ for some finite intermediate }E/\mathbf Q_\ell\}$ on profinite sets, with restriction by precomposition and pointwise operations [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. This is the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient ring, corresponding to the colimit-topology convention in Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Lemma 7.9; it is not the ring of all norm-continuous $\Omega$-valued functions. For every finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ put $R_E(P)=C(P,E)$ with its induced norm topology. The coefficient maps $R_E\to R_\Omega$ are postcomposition with $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$.

A finite scalar local model means a module which on a pro-étale cover has the form $R_T\otimes_{\underline{R(*)}}\underline P$, where $P$ is a finitely presented scalar $R(*)$-module, that is, a cokernel of a map between finite free scalar modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The scalar modules and covers may differ for different terms. For any actual module map $f:L\to M$ between such modules on $S$, write $I_f=\operatorname{im}f$ in the abelian module category, not the closure of a topological image.

Let $h\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose that for every finite intermediate field $E$, every support chain over this $X$, every actual map $g$ between finite scalar local-model $R_{E,S}$-modules, and every affine pro-étale $v:U\to X$,
$$H^qR\Gamma(U,F_{R_E,v}(I_g)[0])=0\quad(q>h).$$
Then for every support chain over $X$, every actual map $f$ between finite scalar local-model $R_{\Omega,S}$-modules, and every affine pro-étale $v:U\to X$,
$$H^qR\Gamma(U,F_{R_\Omega,v}(I_f)[0])=0\quad(q>h).$$
This is preservation of the same uniform upper estimate for the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient ring. No Noetherianity, torsion-cd or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis on $X$ is imposed. Empty schemes, zero maps, identities and the empty chain are included.

The corresponding implication for the ring $P\mapsto C(P,\Omega)$ of all norm-continuous functions is false (already for $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $k$ algebraically closed, $h=0$, the identity map and the empty chain), so this statement does not give that version.

proof.text: Every $T_t$ is qcqs. Start with affine $X$. For a qc open in a qcqs scheme, take a finite affine cover; intersections are qc by [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc], hence it is quasi-separated by the affine-cover criterion. For a closed subscheme, intersect a finite affine cover of the target with it: each piece is affine by the closed-immersion definition, and intersections are closed subsets of the qc intersections of target affines, hence qc. The same criterion applies. This proves the claim inductively along the specified chain, without changing its factorization. In particular $S$ is qcqs. A finitely presented module over the scalar field $Omega$ is finite dimensional: its finite presentation gives finitely many generators, and a maximal independent subfamily is a finite basis. Thus the displayed scalar local models for $L,M$ are finite free, including rank zero. They are lisse in the exact sense of the descent node.

source.place: Lemma 7.9, qcqs hypothesis; elementary scheme-chart and scalar linear-algebra checks

proof.text: Apply lisse descent to $L,M$ on the qcqs scheme $S$, then take a finite compositum of their two coefficient fields, obtaining a common finite field $E$ and lisse $E_S$-modules $L_E,M_E$ whose $R_{Omega,S}$-extensions are $L,M$. Finite scalar extension preserves the local finite-free trivializations. The Hom-surjectivity clause of the same node represents the actual map $f$ by a map $g:L_F	o M_F$ over some finite $Fsupseteq E$. Replace $E$ by $F$. Equality here is equality of the actual module maps after the chosen extension isomorphisms, not merely an identification of their values at geometric points. Each $L_E,M_E$ is an allowed finite scalar local model, so $I_E=operatorname{im}g$ falls under the hypothesis. For every finite $Fsupseteq E$ put $g_F=F_Sotimes_{E_S}g$ and $I_F=operatorname{im}g_F$.

proof.text: Flatness of $F_S/E_S$ and $R_{Omega,S}/E_S$ makes these extensions exact: extension is right exact by its tensor adjunction, and flatness supplies finite limits. Apply extension to the kernel/cokernel description of the image of $g$. This gives $I_Fcong F_Sotimes_{E_S}I_E$ and $I_fcong R_{Omega,S}otimes_{E_S}I_E$. The tail coefficient-colimit node identifies $R_{Omega,S}=arinjlim_{Fsupseteq E}F_S$ as $E_S$-modules with the actual inclusion maps. Relative tensor, defined by its balanced coequalizer and tensor-Hom adjunction, preserves this colimit. Therefore, after restriction to $E_S$, $I_fcongarinjlim_{Fsupseteq E}I_F$. These are sheaf colimits and ordinary abelian images; no closure of an image or norm limit is involved.

Statement-dispute (E7): the base all-continuous form R_Ω=C(P,Ω) is false. Counterexample: X=Spec k with k algebraically closed, h=0. Affine pro-étale tests are Spec LC(P,k), images of finite-E local-model maps are C(−,E)^m, and these are acyclic by finite-normed-scalar-section-acyclicity, so the antecedent holds. The cover from countable-split-profinite-cover, closed F_j exhausting Ω, and a_k∉F_k with a_k→0 give a Čech 1-cocycle with no continuous primitive (double-fibre obstruction, Baire re-checked). Čech H¹ injects into H¹ (Stacks 0A6G), so the conclusion fails for id and the empty chain. The correction to sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed is exactly HRS's colimit-topology Q̄ℓ. It is named under 'Source error' in the report. Every other part of the statement is verbatim against base, and the item is not a target. Proof: steps 1-5 are correct. Step 1: qcqs along the chain, and models are R^n because R_Ω(*)=Ω is a field. Step 2: det-lem lisse descent clauses 1-2 give E and g. Step 3: flatness plus right exactness gives image compatibility, and the tail colimit node gives I_f=colim I_F. Step 4: forget, j_!, v^* as left adjoints, and i_* filtered colimits with a qcqs target and qc complement. Step 5: bounded continuity on qcqs U, Grothendieck → enough injectives, and the module/abelian comparison. h is unchanged. No new nodes. Off-unit tool uses are generic and used as stated.
